title: Historic Plaster Cast Collection — RABASF
institution: Real Academia de Bellas Artes de San Fernando
shortDescription: Conservation and restoration of the historic plaster cast collection at the Real Academia de Bellas Artes de San Fernando. The project is directly associated with the 2004 National Award and the 2005 Europa Nostra Award.
longDescription: This project represents the defining work of Ángeles Solís Parra’s career: the systematic conservation and restoration of the historic plaster cast collection at the Real Academia de Bellas Artes de San Fernando. Works treated include Ariadne, the Stabiae Krater, Farnese Flora, the Gates of Paradise, Venus with the Apple and the Medici Venus. The project required the development of a patented cleaning method — Anjusil® — designed specifically for the complex surface behaviour of historic plaster casts.

title: Archaeological Conservation — Pompeii
shortDescription: Consolidation of archaeological material in the peristyle of the House of the Archaic Diana at Pompeii, with treatment of stone, mortars, ceramics and mosaics.
longDescription: The archaeological material consolidation project took place in the peristyle of the House of the Archaic Diana at Pompeii, with the aim of stabilising the remains, facilitating their study and contributing to the reconstruction of the site. The pieces — stone, mortars, ceramics and mosaics — showed moisture damage, mortar disintegration and microbial growth. Treatment included cleaning, consolidation, fungicidal treatment and gauze facing for subsequent protection, enabling the conservation of the excavated material and its inclusion in the archaeological study and documentation of the site.

title: Plateresque High Altarpiece (1538) — Berzosa de Bureba
shortDescription: Restoration of the Plateresque high altarpiece (1538) in gilded and polychrome wood at the Church of the Assumption of Our Lady in Berzosa de Bureba.
longDescription: The high altarpiece was restored in 1990 with Kipsa. The ensemble, made of gilded and polychrome wood, had significant structural deterioration as well as damage to its sculptures. title: Baroque High Altarpiece (1628–34) — Grandas de Salime
institution: Faculty of Fine Arts, Universidad Complutense de Madrid
shortDescription: Restoration of the Baroque high altarpiece (1628–34) at the Collegiate Church of El Salvador in Grandas de Salime, including structural reassembly and conservation of the polychromy.
longDescription: The high altarpiece was restored in 1993 at the Faculty of Fine Arts, Universidad Complutense de Madrid. The ensemble, made of gilded and polychrome wood, showed deterioration in both its structure and sculptures. Treatment included assembling and anchoring the altarpiece structure to the wall, carpentry, general cleaning, consolidation of the polychromy and constituent materials, fungicidal treatment, reconstruction of missing forms and colour reintegration. In 1993, the village received the Exemplary Town of Asturias Award, in part for the rehabilitation of the Romanesque Collegiate Church of El Salvador, including this altarpiece.

title: Painting Conservation — RABASF Collection
institution: Real Academia de Bellas Artes de San Fernando
shortDescription: Emergency treatment of the painting collection at the Real Academia de Bellas Artes de San Fernando, with works by Alonso Cano and Van Dyck among the documented pieces.
longDescription: Emergency treatment of the paintings held in storage at the Real Academia de Bellas Artes de San Fernando involved nearly fifty oil paintings on canvas affected by moisture, deformed supports, deteriorated stretchers and microbial attack. Treatment included cleaning, stretcher replacement, lining, canvas inserts and consolidation of flaking paint. Alongside stabilising the works, the intervention enabled the identification of hidden signatures and new attributions — including The Virgin and Child with the Repentant Sinners, attributed to Van Dyck, the subject of a dedicated exhibition in Murcia (2011) and a technical study published in Ars Magazine (No. 10, 2011). The collection also includes The Death of Saint Francis of Assisi by Alonso Cano.

title: Painting Collection — Esperanza Parada Pedrosa
institution: Private collection, managed by the family
shortDescription: Conservation and restoration of the painting collection of Esperanza Parada Pedrosa (El Escorial, 1928 — Madrid, 2011), in mixed media on canvas and panel.
longDescription: Between 2017 and 2020, the mixed-media painting collection of Esperanza Parada Pedrosa was conserved and restored in a project managed by the artist’s family. The supports — particularly canvas and panels — showed extensive deterioration, alongside instability in the paint layers resulting from the artist’s complex technique and reuse of materials. Treatment included stretcher replacement, structural treatment of panels, correction of deformations, strip-lining, inserts, cleaning of supports and paint layers, consolidation and colour reintegration. Twenty-six works were restored for exhibitions at the Museo Patio Herreriano and the Museo Ramón Gaya, with further pieces treated in 2020.

title: Anjusil® — Patented Conservation Method
shortDescription: Development, testing and patenting of Anjusil®, a specialised cleaning method for historic plaster cast collections, associated with the 2004 National Award and the Europa Nostra Award.
longDescription: Anjusil® is a compound based on a naturally derived, protein-based film-forming material (natural rubber latex, activated with 0.1% esteramina G), developed by Ángeles Solís Parra to clean historic plaster casts during the restoration of the RABASF collection. The compound rests on the surface of the work without penetrating its structure, acting as a carrier for water and solvents: ammonia dissolves the greasy particles blocking the pores, while water allows foreign substances deposited within them to move. The timed evaporation and coagulation of the latex trap these substances at the surface for subsequent mechanical removal. It is applied with nylon-bristle brushes, which can be washed with water immediately after use. It is used to remove soiling from environmental pollution (dust, smoke and soot), soften old mould-release agents (wax, clay, slip, animal glue and oils) and correct the acidic pH caused by pollution; it also acts as a biocide. Its performance varies according to the material, type of soiling and environmental conditions. It is supplied in 1- and 5-litre containers, in liquid or gel form. Its composition requires personal protective equipment (gloves, goggles and suitable clothing), as it is irritating to the eyes, skin and respiratory tract.

title: National Award 2004 and Europa Nostra Award 2005
shortDescription: National Award for the Restoration and Conservation of Cultural Heritage (2004, Ministry of Culture) and Europa Nostra Award (2005), both associated with the recovery of historic plaster cast collections.
longDescription: In 2004, Ángeles Solís Parra received the Ministry of Culture’s National Award for the Restoration and Conservation of Cultural Heritage in recognition of the work on the RABASF historic plaster cast collection. In 2005, the same project received the Europa Nostra Award, Europe’s most prestigious cultural heritage accolade. These awards affirm the professional and institutional significance of the work and the Anjusil® method at a European level.
